source_text: הֲ/יִנְטֹ֣ר לְ/עוֹלָ֔ם אִם יִשְׁמֹ֖ר לָ/נֶ֑צַח הִנֵּ֥ה דברתי וַ/תַּעֲשִׂ֥י הָ/רָע֖וֹת וַ/תּוּכָֽל־׃פ
english_snapshot: Will he be angry forever? Will he keep it to the end? Look[a], you have spoken, and you have done evil things[c][b], and you have prevailed.

signals.text: The Hebrew consonants of 'you have spoken' can also be read 'I have spoken'; the context favors addressing Judah's own words.

source_text: נָחַ֣ר מַפֻּ֔חַ מ/אשת/ם עֹפָ֑רֶת לַ/שָּׁוְא֙ צָרַ֣ף צָר֔וֹף וְ/רָעִ֖ים לֹ֥א נִתָּֽקוּ׃
english_snapshot: The bellows blow fiercely[a]; the lead is consumed by the fire. In vain the refiner keeps refining[b], but the wicked are not separated out.

signals.text: Or 'The bellows are scorched/burned up; from their fire the lead is consumed.' The Hebrew of this clause is difficult, and translations differ on how the fire and lead are related.

source_text: אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אִם לֹ֥א שרות/ך לְ/ט֑וֹב אִם ל֣וֹא הִפְגַּ֣עְתִּֽי בְ/ךָ֗ בְּ/עֵ֥ת רָעָ֛ה וּ/בְ/עֵ֥ת צָרָ֖ה אֶת הָ/אֹיֵֽב־־׀־־׃
english_snapshot: Yahweh said[a], “Surely I have set you free for good[b]; surely I have made the enemy plead with you in a time of disaster and in a time of distress.”

signals.text: Hebrew uncertain in the first clause; alternatively, 'Surely I have released you for good,' or with a different understanding of the form, 'Surely I have strengthened the remnant for good.'

source_text: וְ/הַֽעֲבַרְתִּי֙ אֶת אֹ֣יְבֶ֔י/ךָ בְּ/אֶ֖רֶץ לֹ֣א יָדָ֑עְתָּ כִּֽי אֵ֛שׁ קָדְחָ֥ה בְ/אַפִּ֖/י עֲלֵי/כֶ֥ם תּוּקָֽד־־׃ס
english_snapshot: And I will make your enemies pass into a land you have not known[a], for a fire has been kindled in my anger; it will burn against you.

signals.text: Or, following some ancient versions and the parallel in Jeremiah 17:4, 'And I will make you serve your enemies in a land you have not known.' The Hebrew consonantal text here reads 'your enemies,' but a different vocalization or Vorlage may underlie the alternate reading.

source_text: מִקְוֵ֤ה יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ יְהוָ֔ה כָּל עֹזְבֶ֖י/ךָ יֵבֹ֑שׁוּ יסור/י בָּ/אָ֣רֶץ יִכָּתֵ֔בוּ כִּ֥י עָזְב֛וּ מְק֥וֹר מַֽיִם חַיִּ֖ים אֶת יְהוָֽה־־־׃ס
english_snapshot: O Yahweh[a], the hope of Israel, all who forsake you will be put to shame; those who turn away from you will be written in the earth, because they have forsaken Yahweh[c][b], the fountain of living waters.

signals.text: Or 'those who turn away from you.' The Hebrew here is textually difficult; the main text follows the Masoretic first-person reading.

source_text: בְּ/רֵאשִׁ֗ית מַמְלֶ֛כֶת יְהוֹיָקִ֥ם בֶּן יֹאושִׁיָּ֖הוּ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה הָיָ֞ה הַ/דָּבָ֤ר הַ/זֶּה֙ אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔ה מֵ/אֵ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה לֵ/אמֹֽר־־׃
english_snapshot: At the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah[a], king of Judah, this word came to Jeremiah from Yahweh, saying[b],

signals.text: Some interpreters note that this verse's reference to Jehoiakim appears difficult in context, since the surrounding material points to Zedekiah (see 27:3, 12).

source_text: וַ/יְהִ֣י בַּ/שָּׁנָ֣ה הַ/הִ֗יא בְּ/רֵאשִׁית֙ מַמְלֶ֨כֶת֙ צִדְקִיָּ֣ה מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה ב/שנת הָֽ/רְבִעִ֔ית בַּ/חֹ֖דֶשׁ הַ/חֲמִישִׁ֑י אָמַ֣ר אֵלַ֡/י חֲנַנְיָה֩ בֶן עַזּ֨וּר הַ/נָּבִ֜יא אֲשֶׁ֤ר מִ/גִּבְעוֹן֙ בְּ/בֵ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה לְ/עֵינֵ֧י הַ/כֹּהֲנִ֛ים וְ/כָל הָ/עָ֖ם לֵ/אמֹֽר׀־־־׃
english_snapshot: And it happened in that year[a], at the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the fourth year, in the fifth month, that Hananiah son of Azzur, the prophet from Gibeon, spoke to me in the house of Yahweh, in the sight of the priests and all the people, saying[b],

signals.text: The Hebrew text says both 'at the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah' and 'in the fourth year.' The translation preserves this wording rather than harmonizing it.

source_text: וְ/לַ/כֹּהֲנִים֙ הַ/לְוִיִּ֔ם לֹֽא יִכָּרֵ֥ת אִ֖ישׁ מִ/לְּ/פָנָ֑/י מַעֲלֶ֨ה עוֹלָ֜ה וּ/מַקְטִ֥יר מִנְחָ֛ה וְ/עֹ֥שֶׂה זֶּ֖בַח כָּל הַ/יָּמִֽים־־־׃ס
english_snapshot: And the Levitical priests will never lack a man before me to offer burnt offerings, burn grain offerings, and make sacrifices continually[a].

signals.text: Jeremiah 33:14-26 is absent from the ancient Greek version of Jeremiah.

source_text: וַ/יֵּ֤שֶׁב יִרְמְיָ֨הוּ֙ בַּ/חֲצַ֣ר הַ/מַּטָּרָ֔ה עַד י֖וֹם אֲשֶׁר נִלְכְּדָ֣ה יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְ/הָיָ֕ה כַּ/אֲשֶׁ֥ר נִלְכְּדָ֖ה יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם־־ס׃פ
english_snapshot: And Jeremiah remained in the court of the guard until the day Jerusalem was captured[b][a]. And it happened when Jerusalem was captured—

signals.text: The Hebrew ends abruptly: 'And it happened when Jerusalem was captured—' This likely functions as a transition into the following material rather than a complete sentence by itself.

source_text: וַ/יְהִ֡י כַּ/אֲשֶׁ֣ר רָ֠אָ/ם צִדְקִיָּ֨הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָ֜ה וְ/כֹ֣ל אַנְשֵׁ֣י הַ/מִּלְחָמָ֗ה וַֽ֠/יִּבְרְחוּ וַ/יֵּצְא֨וּ לַ֤יְלָה מִן הָ/עִיר֙ דֶּ֚רֶךְ גַּ֣ן הַ/מֶּ֔לֶךְ בְּ/שַׁ֖עַר בֵּ֣ין הַ/חֹמֹתָ֑יִם וַ/יֵּצֵ֖א דֶּ֥רֶךְ הָ/עֲרָבָֽה־׀־׃
english_snapshot: And when Zedekiah king of Judah and all the men of war saw them[a], they fled and went out by night from the city by way of the king’s garden, through the gate between the two walls[b]; and he went out by way of the Arabah.

signals.text: Hebrew has 'he went out' in the final clause, though some translations smooth this to 'they went out' to match the earlier plural verbs.

source_text: וַ/יֵּלְכ֗וּ וַ/יֵּֽשְׁבוּ֙ בְּ/גֵר֣וּת כמו/הם אֲשֶׁר אֵ֖צֶל בֵּ֣ית לָ֑חֶם לָ/לֶ֖כֶת לָ/ב֥וֹא מִצְרָֽיִם־׃
english_snapshot: So they went and stayed at Geruth Chimham[a], which is beside Bethlehem[b], intending to go on into Egypt.

signals.text: The written form in the provided text appears irregular; context supports the proper name 'Chimham,' known from 2 Samuel 19:37–40 and associated with a site near Bethlehem.

source_text: עֲלִ֤י גִלְעָד֙ וּ/קְחִ֣י צֳרִ֔י בְּתוּלַ֖ת בַּת מִצְרָ֑יִם לַ/שָּׁוְא֙ הרביתי רְפֻא֔וֹת תְּעָלָ֖ה אֵ֥ין לָֽ/ךְ־׃
english_snapshot: Go up to Gilead and get balm[a], virgin daughter of Egypt. In vain you have multiplied remedies[b]; there is no healing for you.

signals.text: Or 'To no avail you have used many remedies.' The Hebrew verb form in 'you have multiplied' is textually and morphologically difficult in the consonantal text, but the sense in context is clear: Egypt's many treatments are futile.

source_text: לָ/כֵ֞ן הִנֵּ֖ה יָמִ֤ים בָּאִים֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה וְ/שִׁלַּחְתִּי ל֥/וֹ צֹעִ֖ים וְ/צֵעֻ֑/הוּ וְ/כֵלָ֣י/ו יָרִ֔יקוּ וְ/נִבְלֵי/הֶ֖ם יְנַפֵּֽצוּ־־־׃
english_snapshot: Therefore behold[a], days are coming, declares Yahweh, when I will send to him pourers, and they will pour him out[c][b]; they will empty his vessels and shatter their jars.

signals.text: Hebrew 'their jars.' Some interpreters expect 'his jars' by sense, referring to Moab; the received text reads 'their.'

source_text: מִ/בְּכִ֨י יַעְזֵ֤ר אֶבְכֶּה לָּ/ךְ֙ הַ/גֶּ֣פֶן שִׂבְמָ֔ה נְטִֽישֹׁתַ֨יִ/ךְ֙ עָ֣בְרוּ יָ֔ם עַ֛ד יָ֥ם יַעְזֵ֖ר נָגָ֑עוּ עַל קֵיצֵ֥/ךְ וְ/עַל בְּצִירֵ֖/ךְ שֹׁדֵ֥ד נָפָֽל־־־׃
english_snapshot: With the weeping of Jazer I weep for you[a], vine of Sibmah; your branches crossed the sea; they reached as far as Jazer[c][b]. Upon your summer fruit and upon your grape harvest the destroyer has fallen.

signals.text: The Hebrew reads 'they reached as far as the sea of Jazer.' Because Jazer was inland, some understand this as poetic hyperbole, while others propose a textual adjustment such as 'they reached as far as Jazer.'

source_text: נֻסוּ֩ נֻּ֨דוּ מְאֹ֜ד הֶעְמִ֧יקוּ לָ/שֶׁ֛בֶת יֹשְׁבֵ֥י חָצ֖וֹר נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה כִּֽי יָעַ֨ץ עֲלֵי/כֶ֜ם נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֤ר מֶֽלֶךְ בָּבֶל֙ עֵצָ֔ה וְ/חָשַׁ֥ב עלי/הם מַחֲשָׁבָֽה־־־׃
english_snapshot: Flee! Wander far away! Dwell deep[a], inhabitants of Hazor, declares Yahweh[b], for Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has taken counsel against you and devised a plan against you.

signals.text: The Hebrew shifts from 'against you' to 'against them' at the end of the verse; the translation preserves this change.
